objective: Import the existing IT Management workbook into clean GLPI and OpenProject instances using repeatable, validated, backup-first tooling.

in: Back up both applications before import
Verify record counts and application health

constraints: Do not modify the source workbook
Do not expose personal data or credentials in logs
Back up application databases and data before mutation
Imports must be rerunnable without duplicating records

acceptanceCriteria.text: The workbook is normalized successfully and source record counts are documented without exposing sensitive values.
OpenProject contains workbook-derived users, groups, tickets, printers, and equipment records in the IT Management System project without demo data.
GLPI contains mapped workbook employees, tickets, printers, and equipment records without sample data or duplicates.
Both services remain healthy after import and destination counts reconcile with normalized source counts or documented mapping exceptions.
Current database and application backups exist with checksums before import.

assessment.reason: This changes persistent data in two applications and requires cross-schema mapping, idempotency, backups, and reconciliation.
unknowns: Workbook field quality and duplicate keys
GLPI 11 model requirements for each asset type

practices.practice: Create verified pre-import backups before persistent mutations.
Use deterministic source keys and update-or-create semantics.
Compare normalized source and destination counts and sample mapped fields.
practices.reason: Detects silent loss or mapping errors.

obligations.text: Create database and application-data backups for GLPI and OpenProject with SHA-256 checksums before import.
Verify deterministic keys and confirm a second import does not increase destination counts.
Record source counts, destination counts, mapping exceptions, and endpoint/container health.
